Thanks, but any specific data re the current tests, as opposed to all tests? Even before theis new stuff I have been seeing 100ms+ overall.

This is the ongoing tension between unit tests, which by definition test a single unit and are lightning fast, and integration tests which test a bunch of stuff and hence take longer.

Unit tests, again by definition, typically exclude (or mock etc) all other (slow) code except the unit under test.

Imagine that as the testing regime grows, based on somewhere between 5000 and 10000 classes in FreeCAD, there might be eg 50000 tests. To be useful in a TDD environment they must complete quickly. Most of the current unit tests register < 0mS, but some pop up at eg 100 ms. Currently there are only hundreds of tests. Extrapolate this to ... There is MUCH information on the net.

The danger is that the tests take so long to run that they are NOT run. If you are working on a new piece of code it is useful to run tests VERY often, so you know straight away when a change has broken something else. This is why unit tests must run at lightning speed. Once you have experienced this way of working I can assure you you'll never go back.

I have no objection per se to integration tests. They have their place, but I keep arguing for them to be separate as they serve a different purpose which is assuring various units work well together.

This may not be a big impact now, but will become increasingly important over time.

In terms of how to address this, assuming the tests run slower than ideal, again there is much literature. This is not throretical clap trap, but industry standard.

There should be exactly 16 digits in that number I wrote :). This issue happens because of how floats are stored in binary. What is a neatly ending decimal can very well have a recurring binary notation, which is truncated. When printing with all the decimal digits, this truncation can give different numbers.

You can try this, for example (using half-precision for exaggeration to make the point):

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> print("%1.16g"%np.half(12.0300))
12.03125
```

argv: ['/Applications/FreeCAD.app/Contents/Resources/bin/freecad']
```
made me realize, that macOS does not always use command line arguments to pass the filepath.
For `.app` bundles with an "Info.plist" file, the app will receive a special QFileOpenEvent event, see [here](https://stackoverflow.com/a/73577429) and [here](https://doc.qt.io/qt-5/qfileopenevent.html).
FreeCAD receives and processes these events [here](https://github.com/FreeCAD/FreeCAD/blob/b1e521743b359ce02ca8526efbed2feb6331dd4f/src/Gui/GuiApplication.cpp#L152).

How could this cause the errors?

First I show some notes of how files are opened when passed as command line arguments:
```
>> src/Main/MainGui.cpp, int main( int argc, char ** argv )
    ...
    App::Application::Config()["RunMode"] = "Gui";
    ...
    App::Application::init(argc, argv);
    >> src/App/Application.cpp, void Application::init(int argc, char ** argv)
        ...
        initConfig(argc,argv);  --> intializes Python
        initApplication();
        >> src/App/Application.cpp, void Application::initApplication()
        Base::Interpreter().runString(Base::ScriptFactory().ProduceScript("FreeCADInit")); --> runs FreeCADInit.py
        ...
    ...
    Gui::Application::runApplication();
    >> src/Gui/Application.cpp, void Application::runApplication()
        ...
        GUISingleApplication mainApp(argc, App::Application::GetARGV());
        ...
        initOpenInventor();
        ...
        runInitGuiScript();
        >> src/Gui/Application.cpp, void Application::runInitGuiScript()
            Base::Interpreter().runString(Base::ScriptFactory().ProduceScript("FreeCADGuiInit")); --> runs FreeCADGuiInit.py
        ...
        // gets called once we start the event loop
        QTimer::singleShot(0, &mw, SLOT(delayedStartup()));
        ...
        Base::Console().Log("Init: Executing event loop...\n");
        mainApp.exec();
        ...


src/Gui/MainWindow.cpp, void MainWindow::delayedStartup()
    ...
    std::list<std::string> files = App::Application::getCmdLineFiles();
    files = App::Application::processFiles(files);
    >> src/App/Application.cpp, std::list<std::string> Application::processFiles(...)
        ...
        Application::_pcSingleton->openDocument(file.filePath().c_str());
        >> src/App/Application.cpp, Document* Application::openDocument(...)
            ...
            auto docs = openDocuments(filenames, nullptr, nullptr, nullptr, createView);
            >> src/App/Application.cpp, std::vector<Document*> Application::openDocuments(...)
                ...
                auto doc = openDocumentPrivate(path, name.c_str(), label, isMainDoc, createView, std::move(objNames));
                >> src/App/Application.cpp, Document* Application::openDocumentPrivate(const char * FileName, ...)
                    ... reads the file into a new document
    ...
```
That means, files are opened in `delayedStartup()` after `FreeCADInit.py` and `FreeCADGuiInit.py` are executed.

For the .app in macOS, the files are opened in the event handler:
```
>> src/Gui/GuiApplication.cpp, bool GUIApplication::event(QEvent * ev)
    ...
    Application::Instance->open(fn, "FreeCAD");
    >> src/Gui/Application.cpp, void Application::open(const char* FileName, const char* Module)
        ...
        Command::doCommand(Command::App, "FreeCAD.openDocument('%s')", unicodepath.c_str());
        >> [via macro] src/Gui/Command.cpp, void Command::_doCommand(const char *file, int line, DoCmd_Type eType, const char* sCmd, ...)
            ...
            _runCommand(file,line,eType,format.constData());
            >> src/Gui/Command.cpp, void Command::_runCommand(const char *file, int line, DoCmd_Type eType, const char* sCmd)
                ...
                Base::Interpreter().runString(sCmd);
```
There is no instance of the `GUIApplication`. But there is an instance of `GUISingleApplication mainApp` that can be seen in the very first code block. (The heritage order is `QApplication > GUIApplicationNativeEventAware > GUIApplication > GUISingleApplication`.)
So `mainApp` is created between the execution of `FreeCADInit.py` and `FreeGuiCADInit.py`. This should not be a problem normally, because the event loop (`mainApp.exec();`) is started after everything else is finished.
As far as I have seen by using breakpoints, `bool GUIApplication::event(QEvent * ev)` is called several times before the event loop is started with specific events.

This makes me wonder, if this function is maybe also called with a `QFileOpenEvent`.
So I just tried to run the following code block in function `Application::runApplication()` (file src/Gui/Application.cpp).

```
{
    QString file = QString::fromStdString("/filepath/of/demo.FCStd");
    QByteArray fn = file.toUtf8();
    Application::Instance->open(fn, "FreeCAD");
}
```

When I inserted the block before `initOpenInventor();`, then FreeCAD crashed during start-up with a segmentation fault in libCoin.
When I inserted the block after that line and before `runInitGuiScript();`, I had the same behaviour as in berebin's videos.
And when I inserted the block after `runInitGuiScript();`, everything worked normally without any errors.


On my Linux system I cannot dig deeper into this issue -- this will need someone with a FreeCAD build environment on a macOS computer.
I recommend to first check if and why the QFileOpenEvent is handled before `runInitGuiScript();` is executed.
Remember that `QFileOpenEvent` is only issued for `.app` bundles.

I think, the problem could be fixed by adding a single-shot QTimer in the handler for the QFileOpenEvent, similar to `MainWindow::delayedStartup()` so that the file will be opened after the event loop is running (and not before).

Hi @SimoneMaffei98!
I think there is a misunderstanding.

When running a Python script, it is normal that the execution is interrupted on an unhandled error (see [here in the Python tutorial](https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/errors.html)). When you run a FreeCAD macro, it will also be interrupted on the first unhandled error.

The FreeCAD Python Console is not for running scripts that way. When you insert your code lines in FreeCAD's Python Console via Copy&Paste, then each code block (a single line or a single line followed by indented lines) is executed separately. So you are running not a single script with 100 lines but 100 single-line scripts and after every execution of a script, you see the result or the error that made it abort the execution.

You can try this yourself:
Run this code in the Python Console and you will get your expected results -- everything will be executed even after previous errors.
```
print(1)
x1 = 1 / 0
print(2)
x2 = 2 / 0
print(3)

```

Now, let's modify the code a bit, so that it is still the same:
```
if True:
    print(1)
    x1 = 1 / 0
    print(2)
    x2 = 2 / 0
    print(3)

```
If you run this again in the FreeCAD Python Console, then only the first `1` will be printed. This is only one code block that is executed, so one small script that behaves normally and aborts on the first division by zero.

Another example: The following code is absolutely valid Python code, but it will not execute in FreeCAD Python Console (Error invalid syntax).
```
if True:
    print(1)
print(2)
```
This is because you cannot run two code blocks in the FreeCAD Python Console in one execution. If you insert an empty line before the last line, it will work again, because then it is two separate code blocks.


So this is not a bug. If you just want to automatically execute each line separately, then there are ways to do it, depending on how your scripts look like (e.g. only single line commands).

OK, was a long journey but finally found the culprit.
The `isFile()` function of `FileInfo` uses an "optimistic" implementation that freezes FC on specific files.
When a file is saved using `FCBak`, the whole folder content list is tested (each item is tested to be a file or not).
In case of tests, this is the `/tmp/` folder and it happens that CI shall have in this folder some very specific file(s) that makes the `isFile()` function to freeze.
Didn't investigate deeper (enough time consumed :smile: ).
Once #9974 is merged, this one can be cleaned up and CI should pass. :wink:
